text:
jessica: Heads-up — we saw a flurry of GPU node transient errors in us-west-2 this morning, lots of short-lived network timeouts that trigged paging. wondering if we should change grouping or thresholds for these network+oom combos.

sam: saw that. most were <30s and auto-recovered. paging on each one is noisy.

kevin: what percentage were repeat-failures vs one-offs? if duplicates hit the same node within 5m that's worth paging.

jessica: ~82% were single short blips, 10% reappeared within 10m, 8% escalated to pod restarts.

nguyen: proposal: ticket for single short blip, page if same node has 3 failures within 10m or if downstream SLO breach observed. simpler and reduces wakeups.

sam: agree. also add cardinality grouping: if failures affect >5 nodes in a fleet in 1m, page immediately (could be network fabric).

kevin: +1 on grouping. we should also consider impact on user-facing p95 latency. if p95 spikes > 200ms for >2m, force-page regardless of counts.

jessica: here's a sample Prom rule I sketched for debouncing:

```
ALERT GPU_Node_Transient
  IF increase(gpu_node_network_errors_total[1m]) >= 1
  FOR 5m
  LABELS {severity="warning"}
  ANNOTATIONS {summary="Transient GPU network error"}
```

and a higher severity rule that aggregates cardinality:

```
ALERT GPU_Fleet_MultiNode_Network
  IF count_over_time((gpu_node_network_errors_total > 0)[1m]) > 5
  FOR 1m
  LABELS {severity="page"}
```

nguyen: the debounced FOR 5m will lower noise but hide short bursts. maybe use two rules: one immediate with severity=info that files a ticket, and one with FOR 1m+ and cardinality for paging.

sam: we should also implement a mute window for scheduled maintenance and autoscaler churn windows. currently scaling churn causes tons of errors.

jessica: good point — add a recording rule to detect autoscale windows and add mute label to alerts via alertmanager: `mute=autoscale` when cluster_scaling_active == 1.

kevin: ops-bot can we add a Grafana alert that correlates p95 latency + node error cardinality so pages only when both criteria met?

ops-bot: @kevin scheduled: created composite alert "GPU_Fleet_Impact" that requires p95_latency > 200ms AND count(node_errors)>3 in 2m. Will appear in next deploy. :white_check_mark:

jessica: cost note — keeping long FOR windows increases ticket backlog but reduces paging; we should tune by service SLA. infra services can be tolerant, product-facing routes should be stricter.

nguyen: action items: 1) implement two-tier rules (ticket vs page) 2) add cardinality-based page rule 3) add mute when autoscaling 4) add composite p95+cardinality alert for product lanes.

sam: i'll open the PR with example Prom rules + alertmanager silence automation.

jessica: thanks — please also add a short playbook for oncall: quick checks (region network health, recent scaling events, rollback path). keep it <6 steps.

kevin: tagging @oncall-sre so this lands in runbook.

oncall-sre: noted. will add runbook and run a 48h pilot with new thresholds on staging before rolling to prod.

jessica: perfect. if staging holds we'll roll to us-west-2 only and monitor noise reduction metrics (pager counts per day, median time-to-resolve).

sam: ping me once PR is ready, i'll review tonight. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks team.
